name: Erebos Up
lines: river of hate, by which the gods swear
river of forgetting

The Styx winds nine times round the underworld (Hesiod, Theogony 790-792). When the gods swear an oath, Iris brings a jug of its water, and a god who swears falsely by it lies breathless for a year and is shut out of the gods' councils for nine more (Theogony 775-806).
Here its violet water runs down past the thrones to meet the others.

Lethe, forgetting. Plato's Myth of Er: souls about to be born again cross the burning Plain of Forgetfulness and drink from the River of Unmindfulness, and forget everything (Republic 621a). Virgil puts the Lethe in Elysium, where the souls drink 'the waters that free from care' (Aeneid 6.713-715).
Do not drink. Poppies, the flower of sleep, grow along it outside.
Cocytus, the river of wailing. Homer: 'Pyriphlegethon and Cocytus, which is a branch of the water of Styx, flow into Acheron, at a rock where the two roaring rivers meet' (Odyssey 10.513-515).
It runs cold; ice floats on it outside.

Pyriphlegethon, the river of fire. Plato says it pours into a great place burning with fire and makes a lake boiling with water and mud, then circles round under the earth (Phaedo 113a-b). Outside it rings the walls of Tartarus.
Here it is led in through the east wall, still burning.

Acheron, the river of woe, which Charon crosses with the dead in his boat for an obol. Plato: it flows through desert places and under the earth into the Acherusian Lake, where the souls of most of the dead come (Phaedo 112e-113a).
Its murky green water comes in through the south wall.
Where the five rivers meet
before the throne of Hades

The five rivers of the underworld come into the king's hall through five culverts in the walls: the Styx and the Lethe from behind the thrones, the Cocytus from the west, the Phlegethon burning from the east, the Acheron from the south.
Here they run together round the hearth of blue fire, violet, white, ice-blue, fire and green, and do not mix.
Homer has rivers meeting below too: 'Pyriphlegethon and Cocytus, a branch of the water of Styx, flow into Acheron, at a rock where the two roaring rivers meet' (Odyssey 10.513-515).

👑 The Palace of Hades. The great hall: four black columns round a hearth of blue-white fire, the throne of the Unseen King. The five rivers of the underworld come in through the walls and meet in a ring round the hearth. Doors lead off to the banquet hall (west), the treasury (east), the Hall of Orpheus (north), and beyond the banquet hall, the Chairs of Forgetfulness.
Hades, the Unseen King
Persephone, queen of the dead
You smell of sunlight. It has been a long winter for my mother, I think. Sit with me a little, and tell me what is flowering up there.
empty: the queen is above

It is her season above. Persephone went up to her mother Demeter at the spring equinox, and the earth flowered; she comes down again at the autumn equinox (22 September), and then the earth goes bare.
The Homeric Hymn to Demeter: because she ate the pomegranate seeds, she must spend part of every year below with Hades, and the rest above with her mother.
Where the queen sits
The chair by the loom is empty. It is her season below: Persephone is in the great hall of the palace, on her throne beside Hades.

The chair by the loom is empty and the lamps are low. It is her season above: Persephone went up to her mother Demeter at the spring equinox, and comes down again at the autumn equinox (22 September).
The queen herself is in the great hall, on her throne.
The queen is above with her mother Demeter until the autumn equinox.
for the songs of spring
Persephone's own lyre. Orpheus played here, too, when he came for Eurydice; it was Persephone, Ovid says, who could not refuse him (Metamorphoses 10.46-49).
Her dressing table
a bronze mirror, scent
A mirror of polished bronze, little jars of scented oil, a comb of ivory. When Psyche came down for a box of Persephone's beauty, it was from here the queen filled it (Apuleius, The Golden Ass 6.20).
